package_info.package_versions: 8.0.1 (and any version published under these names)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are copycat versions of the legitimate 'mitmproxy' library, but with critical security safeguards deliberately removed from the web API. This introduces an artificial remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability, allowing any user on the same network to execute arbitrary code on the host running the mitmproxy web interface. The packages are designed to appear as legitimate or newer versions, increasing the risk of accidental adoption by unsuspecting developers.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when mitmproxy web interface is started)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code disables all cross-origin protections on the mitmproxy web API, allowing any origin to send requests with any headers and methods, which enables unauthenticated remote code execution via the API.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling all CORS protections on a sensitive API exposes the application to remote code execution by any network peer, which is a critical security vulnerability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to restrict API access to trusted origins and authenticated users; the malicious code removes these safeguards, allowing anyone on the network to access and exploit the API.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In rare cases, open CORS headers might be used for public APIs with no sensitive operations, but never for APIs capable of code execution.
key_indicators: Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to '*' on a sensitive API
Access-Control-Allow-Methods includes POST and DELETE without authentication

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when mitmproxy web interface is started)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code disables the X-Frame-Options header, allowing the web interface to be embedded in iframes, which can facilitate clickjacking and further exploitation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling X-Frame-Options on an administrative interface increases the risk of clickjacking attacks, which can be used to trick users into performing unintended actions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to set X-Frame-Options to 'DENY' or 'SAMEORIGIN' for admin interfaces; commenting this out removes a key security control.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some public-facing sites may allow framing for embedding, but never for sensitive admin APIs.
key_indicators: No replacement or alternative protection provided

attack_chain.action: User installs and runs the malicious mitmproxy2 or mitmproxy-iframe package, believing it to be a legitimate or newer version.
attack_chain.leads_to: Web interface is started with weakened security controls.

attack_chain.action: The web API is exposed with all CORS protections disabled and X-Frame-Options header removed.
attack_chain.leads_to: Any user on the same network can send arbitrary requests to the API.

attack_chain.action: An attacker on the same network sends a crafted HTTP request to the exposed API, triggering remote code execution on the victim's machine.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains code execution on the victim's system.

behavioral_signatures: mitmproxy web interface running with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
mitmproxy web interface missing X-Frame-Options header
Unrestricted CORS headers on sensitive local web APIs
file_indicators: mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py with commented out or missing X-Frame-Options
network_indicators: mitmproxy web interface accessible from any origin
Unusual POST/DELETE requests to mitmproxy API from non-local origins
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for mitmproxy installations where the web interface responds with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and lacks the X-Frame-Options header. Scan for package names like 'mitmproxy2' or 'mitmproxy-iframe' in dependency manifests. Review mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py for commented out or missing security headers. Alert on any mitmproxy API endpoints that accept unauthenticated requests from non-local origins.
